findings.evidence: TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AugmentationPoint/ConnectedComponent.lean:66 `connectedComponentIdeal_kernelPoint_le_ker` and :52 `map_connectedComponentIdempotent_kernelPoint_eq_one` both name the point; the statements here fix `show PrimeSpectrum H from Bialgebra.augmentationPoint k H` (lines 148, 163, 177).
findings.fix: Put the point in the names, as the adjacent file already does: `antipode_augmentationPoint_mem_connectedComponentIdeal` / `..._iff` / `map_connectedComponentIdeal_augmentationPoint_...`.
findings.issue: `antipode_mem_connectedComponentIdeal` (and `antipode_mem_connectedComponentIdeal_iff`, line 161, and `map_connectedComponentIdeal_antipodeAlgHom`, line 174) name no point, so they advertise a statement about `PrimeSpectrum.connectedComponentIdeal x` for any `x`; the statements hold only at `Bialgebra.augmentationPoint k H` and are false for a general point.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean:724 `Ideal.comap_map_eq_self_of_isMaximal`, :359 `Ideal.map_comap_eq_self_of_equiv` — `_eq_self` is the standard marker for a map fixing an ideal.
findings.issue: `map_connectedComponentIdeal_antipodeAlgHom` describes only the left-hand term `Ideal.map antipodeAlgHom I`; nothing in the name says the ideal is fixed, so the name reads like a definition rather than an equality with `I`.

findings.evidence: Naming conventions, "Predicates as suffixes": `_involutive` for `Involutive f`; mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean:280 `inv_involutive : Function.Involutive (Inv.inv)` vs. the pointwise `inv_inv`; mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/GroupLike.lean:54 uses `antipode_antipode` for exactly this pointwise shape.
findings.fix: Rename to `antipode_antipode`, or restate as `Function.Involutive` and keep the name.
findings.issue: `antipode_involutive` carries the `_involutive` predicate suffix but states the pointwise equation `antipode (antipode x) = x`, not `Function.Involutive (antipode k : H → H)`.

findings.evidence: TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/Augmentation.lean:34 `abbrev augmentationPoint`, documented at :18 as "the point of the affine spectrum defined by the counit"; lines 148/163/177 of this file use that name directly.
findings.fix: Name the abbrev `augmentationPoint` (or drop it and use `Bialgebra.augmentationPoint k H` throughout) and rename the helper lemma accordingly.
findings.issue: `augmentationPrime` invents a second name for an object the repo already calls `augmentationPoint`, and that terminology propagates into `antipodeAlgEquiv_mem_augmentationPrime_iff` (line 102) while the public statements spell out `Bialgebra.augmentationPoint`, leaving two names for one thing in one file.

summary: The three public names omit the point the connected-component ideal is taken at, so they read as statements about an arbitrary `connectedComponentIdeal` when they hold only at the augmentation point; the ideal-map lemma also gives no hint of its conclusion. Two private names deviate from established conventions (`_involutive`, `augmentationPoint`).
